question.problem: For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\text{Var}[X]=0.1,$ $\text{Var}[Y]=0.7,$ and $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.2.$ Find $\text{Var}[7X-4Y].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables, and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y]+2ab\,\text{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[7X-4Y] & ={7}^{2}\cdot 0.1+(-4)^{2}\cdot 0.7+2\cdot 7\cdot (-4)\cdot 0.2 \\  & =4.9+11.2-11.2 \\  & =4.9.\end{aligned}
$$
